## Where did the space go? (Alt+W)

**Alt+W** opens the new **Usage view**: the folders and files of a branch by
the space they take, largest first, with a bar and their share of the folder.
Enter goes into a folder, down to what fills the disk; the panel on the right
shows the item's size on the disk and apparent, number of files and date.
One disk at a time (other file systems are marked `>` and left out), hard
links counted once, and the space on the disk as `du` counts it (`A` switches
to the apparent size). The bars take the color of their share: up to 10%, up
to 40%, more.

![The Usage view of a home folder: an old backup file at the top with 37%, then the projects, videos and downloads folders](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andrelnfernandes/xylem/v0.4.0/docs/screenshots/usage-vivid.png)

In the tree, **Alt+K → Percent** shows each folder's share of the one above,
with a colored bar against its largest sibling.

## Remote machines over SSH

Type `user@host:/path` (or `ssh://user@host:port/path`) in **L** (Log), or
give it to `xy`, and browse that machine's files as a tree, alone or next to
this one with F8. Xylem speaks SFTP through your own `ssh`, so
`~/.ssh/config`, keys, the agent and `known_hosts` all apply, and nothing is
installed on the other side; passwords and host keys are asked in the
footer. The viewer, search, Compare and Copy (to this machine) work there,
and **Alt+X** opens a shell on the remote machine, with the tree following
its `cd`. The remote side is read-only for now.

## Google Drive, S3 and other cloud storage, through rclone

Mount them with [rclone](https://rclone.org) and Xylem works there like on
any folder. On Linux, the DISK panel, Info and Avail say which service a
mounted folder is (Google Drive, Amazon S3, OneDrive...). The new manual page
explains the setup, what is different on a mounted remote, and how to find
what fills a Google Drive before buying more storage.

## New themes: slate, graphite, daylight and vivid

In the style of Windows Terminal (slate) and of macOS in dark and light mode
(graphite, daylight), and **vivid**: strong colors on a deep indigo, for
presentations, videos and screenshots (the one above). Twelve themes in all,
in F4 or with `theme = "..."`; each has its own colors for the bars
(`bar_low`, `bar_mid`, `bar_high`, which `[colors]` can change too).

## Smaller things

- **E** no longer opens binary files in the text editor: the new `[editors]`
  table in `config.toml` chooses a program by file name, and binary files
  without one are refused, with a hint to use **O**.
- `xy --man` shows the formatted manual page in a terminal; redirected to a
  file, it still writes the source, for installing it.
- The Alt menu in the footer lists Alt+W.

## Install

Download the archive for your system below (Linux x86_64 or ARM64, static;
Windows x86_64), or `cargo install xylem-fm`. The website:
https://andrelnfernandes.github.io/xylem/
